newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Apple Fields announces leasing plans.
newsitem.headline: Apple Fields announces leasing plans.

text.p: Listed orchardist Apple Fields on Thursday announced an agreement to lease out most of its Christchurch orchards to a subsidiary of unlisted public company Scales Corporation Ltd until the end of June.

Apple Fields said in December it would quit orcharding and restructure into a residential property development company, after the Apple and Pear Marketing Board (NZAPMB) turned down its application to export all of its own fruit.
Scales is employing Hawkes Bay contact manager and horticultural consultants Rex Graham & Associates to undertake the management of the orchards and the packing of the fruit.
Jobs managing and running the orchards and the packing centre for this season are being offered to ex Apple Fields staff, and also to part-time staff for thinning, picking and packing.
The crops will be sold through the Apple and Pear Board.
Apple Fields said in December it was not prepared to continue to accept the risk to income and capital which the board's present structure represented.
"However, this arrangement enables the company to realise benefits from the present crop," the company said on Thursday.

It said that over the last few years Scales had gained considerable experience in shipping and trading of apples. It had pioneered, in conjunction with the Apple and Pear Board, the export of apples to the Pacific seaboard of Russia.
Apple Fields managing director Tom Kain told Reuters the lease applied to 17 of Apple Fields' 19 mid-Canterbury orchards.
Asked what the company's plans for the remaining two orchards were, Kain replied: "We understand there are people interested in those."

Asked what will happen after the lease expires in June, Kain said: "Our intention is to move on now with the property development. We don't see a future for this type of corporate orchardist under the Apple and Pear Board."
He said the lease arrangements were confidential, "but obviously our remuneration comes through the lease".

Kain said in the event of a legislation change that allowed Apple Fields to export all its own crop independent of the NZAPMB, the company had the necessary managerial and marketing skills to re-enter orcharding.
